title: Honest Interval Length for Marginal Median Contrasts under Blocking with Two Classification Defects
banked_reason: Math referee PASS; the required completion comparison and stopping modulus remain open, and the delivered finite-program theorem falls below the field novelty floor.
gap_reasons: The proposed deliverable is an evaluated sharp all-large-n positive-defect limit (or exhaustive evaluated subsequential set), but this theorem supplies only fixed-n mesh computability and an expressly unevaluated compact cluster set; the required completion comparison and stopping modulus remain open.

The positioning does not establish theorem-level novelty for the substituted generic finite rational grid/enclosure result against the closest finite-population confidence-set and finite-decision-program literature; broad informed-by distinctions do not make this non-asymptotic computational observation the promised mathematical contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: Three solve rounds audited the restricted certificates, attempted conditional-disclosure completion comparison, and delivered a total globally honest full-record grid rule with certified scaled minimax excess at most 1/q. The sharp positive-defect value and PC2 stopping modulus remain open; legal remote coding defeats deletion/common-bridge shortcuts. D0.5 math passed, but the substituted finite-program result achieved incremental rather than field novelty; no Lean formalization was launched.
tldr: For the fixed-cohort causal contrast of left marginal medians under exact balanced blocked assignment, every public integer precision \(q\ge1\) yields a canonical total original-record interval with \(9/10\) coverage on the full \(\mathcal C_n(N)\) and scaled worst length within \(1/q\) of \(nL_n(2)\). A positive rational requested accuracy \(\epsilon\) is met by \(q\ge\lceil1/\epsilon\rceil\). Exact rational lower certificates and matching lifted-rule upper certificates make the finite-size minimax value a uniformly computable real. For every public computable schedule \(q_n\to\infty\), the rule risks, minimax values and grid values share a nonempty compact subsequential-value set in \([47/20,\sqrt{1{,}150{,}976}]\). Its elements and any limiting constant remain unevaluated. Effective completion comparison and sharp positive-defect evaluation are open; the restricted \(1/5\) surcharge does not establish full-model separation.
gap: Finite-sample randomization inference for quantiles of individual treatment effects is established by \cite{SuLi2024}; regular marginal-quantile-effect inference and sharp mean-risk reductions address other decision objects. The mathematical gap is an evaluated minimax expected connected length for a contrast of marginal medians, with one membership swap per arm in the risk class and coverage on the full \(\mathcal C_n(N)\). The accessible summary of \cite{SedranskMeyer1978} establishes a direct stratified-quantile precedent; its unavailable full theorem text prevents a definitive historical containment check.
fill: The research target is an evaluated positive-defect completion experiment with effectively matching lower and upper certificates, quantitative legal padding and original-record lifting, and total intervals attaining the solved benchmark. PC2, conditional remote-information control and full-value evaluation remain explicit open obligations. Marginal sampling containment in the historical survey framework supplies a sanity check, not a sharp joint causal-length comparison.
